modifications: Establish a dedicated public Python library over the authenticated online security universe.

Expose online count, catalog generation and publication time, online-security listing, historical exact-ticker resolution, exact public-ID identity resolution, and adjustment-history reads with inclusive date bounds.
Bind each library instance to one authenticated catalog generation and return one generic unavailable result for every public ID outside that online snapshot.
Return typed public security and exact daily-bar values without exposing provider, pipeline, manifest, warning, repair, or offline-state machinery.
Add StandaloneReader and read_alpaca_pricing.py for source-scoped resolved pricing from the standalone downloader/lineage store, without changing DataLibrary's online-catalogue contract.

Consume completed group receipts under shared lineage and sorted pricing locks; report busy by default, reject stale or incomplete handoffs, and never download, acknowledge, repair, copy or re-audit approved inputs.

Resolve reused tickers to every published public ID, require explicit ambiguous-ID selection, apply the established history-source policy, and return exact values with inclusive date filtering as JSON or CSV.
Read completed standalone groups while the lineage worker handles unrelated groups, retaining fail-fast busy behavior and explicit --wait for conflicting work.
Use the shared snapshot handshake and accept lock-compatible lineage v2 receipts after protocol upgrade, without changing identity rules, prices, or DataLibrary's online contract.
Add StandaloneReader.get_histories for ordered, deduplicated adjustment views from one locked group snapshot, reusing decoded physical aliases within the call without persistent caches or writes.

Accept multiple/repeated --type values and --all-types in read_alpaca_pricing.py; multi-view JSON groups bars by adjustment and CSV adds an adjustment column, while default/single-view output retains its existing shape.
Keep compound adjustment names atomic, preserve fully-adjusted --type all semantics, and fail the complete request without partial stdout if a requested view is unavailable or conflicts.

Expose metadata-only standalone source rosters and completed group evidence, including resolved public-ID locators and all latest observed labels, without changing DataLibrary's online catalogue contract.

Allow get_histories to include published evidence from the same locked group snapshot; retain source generations and distinguish lookup metadata and request asof from dated listing facts or adjustment vintage.

Add opt-in bounded generation-keyed RAM caching to StandaloneReader for selected JSON documents and immutable decoded pricing payloads; retain fresh index selection, pricing receipts, pending-work checks and existing lock order on every call.

Expose get_generation for lightweight locked freshness checks without rereading assignment boundaries, and cache_info for in-process memory accounting; preserve returned values and independent mutable result documents.
Reuse assembled adjustment histories within a call only when physical payloads, row selections, labels and overlap policy are identical; raw and adjusted source-selection policies remain distinct.

Add open_group for compact summaries and explicit-ID eight-view reads from one locked group snapshot, using the same history assembly and source policy as existing reads; parse selected lineage documents once per handshake and release working data on close.

Retain a private compact freshness token whose check_current compares current index selections and locked pricing receipts without rereading approved lineage documents; consumer exceptions preserve their type, and closed snapshots cannot serve histories.
Add in-memory read/reuse/eviction counters shared across group caches and conservative tuple/Unicode cache accounting without recursive per-cell traversal.

Reuse locked path selections and timestamp-to-session conversions, and directly assemble uncontested observations; resolve only overlapping timestamps with full source coverage and unchanged source-selection rules, sharing raw/adjusted alias assembly only without source competition.

Retain consumed pricing-receipt file identity in group freshness tokens so unchanged receipts are reused without rereading their JSON; pending-work, index-generation and changed-file checks remain live.

Expose GroupSnapshot.set_cache_limit to resize retained decoded-data reuse between explicit-ID reads within the reader's configured cap, evicting only as needed while preserving source values, aliases, locks and freshness checks.

Include deliberately unavailable auxiliary pricing inputs in standalone snapshot locks and freshness tokens; reject a formerly absent input which gains pricing or pending publication, including cached reads and export checks.
Keep public histories and group summaries scoped to actual published price sources; auxiliary metadata remains operator evidence rather than a fabricated security or empty pricing series.

Trust standalone published paths and digest-selected cached content from first consumption without file metadata probes. Select current source receipts after locks are reacquired, preserving changed-generation, pending-publication and missing-input failures without re-auditing payloads.

Replace DataLibrary repository-root/v6 access with explicit standalone store semantics, exact decimal volumes, observed metadata and generation-bound serving catalogue reads and atomic exports through the shared history engine.
Read bounded source-presence evidence across all selected adjustment views, including unresolved observations and shared physical aliases, for the serving producer.

Accept digit-leading historical labels in DataLibrary ticker resolution, independently of standalone source-locator syntax, while preserving dated matches, ambiguity, normalization and metadata-only lookup from the opened catalogue.

Add catalogue-only CSV export planning and per-public-ID CSV exports with stable logical pricing columns, per-identity column-alias digests, exact numeric values and a final manifest published atomically after all outputs complete.

Consume each selected serving group once, share manifest-selected physical payloads across its identities until their last use, and derive output column aliases in memory without source hashing, filesystem discovery or repeated upstream audits.

Support one through four CSV export workers, defaulting to two, over intact selected groups, sharing one accepted catalogue with bounded dispatch and compact completion messages while preserving per-group source reuse and deterministic output ordering.
Make CSV destination and source locks nonblocking regardless of the reader wait setting; coordinate cancellation, progress and final publication after workers release their resources.

Publish each completed run's final manifest inside its timestamp directory with run-relative identity paths, so completed exports are self-contained and removable without a shared selector or directory discovery.

Hold a store-wide shared operation lock from accepted catalogue generation through CSV final-manifest publication, rejecting a stale DataLibrary or a concurrent store writer without re-auditing upstream data.
Consume the lineage producer's published numerical source selections across all views without repeating source authority decisions; retain dated ticker identity and window-independent history.
